package orchestrator

import (
	"context"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"net"
	"net/http"
	"strings"
	"time"

	"tenant-v4/internal/observability"
	"tenant-v4/internal/protocol"
)

// Server timeouts. Go's net/http default server has no timeouts at all, so
// every one of these is set explicitly on the http.Server the orchestrator
// runs. The orchestrator executes no tasks — it registers, looks up and
// brokers — so its request handling is short and the write budget is
// generous rather than task-sized.
const (
	// ReadHeaderTimeout bounds how long a client may take to send request
	// headers. It is the guard against slow-header connection exhaustion.
	ReadHeaderTimeout = 10 * time.Second

	// ReadTimeout bounds the whole request read, headers and body together.
	// Bodies here are capped at 1 MB (registration, messages, service
	// updates) or 64 KB (channels) by protocol.ReadJSON.
	ReadTimeout = 30 * time.Second

	// WriteTimeout bounds response writing. A full service directory with
	// routing table and namespace map is the largest response served.
	WriteTimeout = 60 * time.Second

	// IdleTimeout bounds how long a keep-alive connection may sit unused.
	IdleTimeout = 120 * time.Second

	// ShutdownGrace bounds graceful shutdown: in-flight requests are given
	// this long to finish before the listener is closed hard.
	ShutdownGrace = 15 * time.Second
)

// muxMethod binds one HTTP method to one handler on a route.
type muxMethod struct {
	method  string
	handler http.HandlerFunc
}

// muxRoute is one path pattern and every method served on it.
type muxRoute struct {
	pattern string
	methods []muxMethod

	// noFallback suppresses the method-less 405 pattern for this route.
	//
	// net/http's ServeMux panics when two patterns overlap and neither is
	// more specific than the other. A method-less literal such as
	// "/v1/admin/operators/register" overlaps "GET /v1/admin/operators/{name}"
	// on GET, and neither contains the other: the literal is narrower in
	// path, the wildcard route narrower in method. Registering both is a
	// startup panic, so literal siblings of a wildcard segment carry only
	// their method-specific routes and fall through to the wildcard's
	// fallback for everything else.
	noFallback bool
}

// allowed lists the methods this route serves, in registration order, for
// the Allow header of a 405 response.
func (r muxRoute) allowed() []string {
	out := make([]string, 0, len(r.methods))
	for _, m := range r.methods {
		out = append(out, m.method)
	}
	return out
}

// routeTable is the orchestrator's complete surface: the protocol endpoints
// from protocol/spec, and the administrative endpoints backed by state this
// component owns — operators, agents, and its own overview. Nothing here
// serves strategies, approvals, observations, workflows or tasks; those
// belong to other components and are absent by design.
//
// Every pattern is an absolute path taken from protocol's path constants. A
// client composes requests as origin + path, so no constant here omits its
// /v1 prefix.
func (o *Orchestrator) routeTable() []muxRoute {
	operators := strings.TrimSuffix(protocol.PathAdminOperators, "/")
	agents := strings.TrimSuffix(protocol.PathAdminAgents, "/")

	return []muxRoute{
		// --- Protocol endpoints ---
		{
			pattern: protocol.PathRegister,
			methods: []muxMethod{
				{method: http.MethodPost, handler: o.HandleRegister},
				{method: http.MethodDelete, handler: o.HandleDeregister},
			},
		},
		{
			pattern: protocol.PathRotateKey,
			methods: []muxMethod{
				{method: http.MethodPost, handler: o.HandleRotateKey},
			},
		},
		{
			pattern: protocol.PathServices,
			methods: []muxMethod{
				{method: http.MethodGet, handler: o.HandleServices},
			},
		},
		{
			pattern: protocol.PathChannel,
			methods: []muxMethod{
				{method: http.MethodPost, handler: o.HandleChannel},
			},
		},
		{
			pattern: protocol.PathHealth,
			methods: []muxMethod{
				{method: http.MethodGet, handler: o.HandleHealth},
			},
		},
		{
			pattern: protocol.PathAudit,
			methods: []muxMethod{
				{method: http.MethodGet, handler: o.HandleAudit},
			},
		},

		// --- Observability ---
		{
			pattern: protocol.PathMetrics,
			methods: []muxMethod{
				{method: http.MethodGet, handler: o.HandleMetrics},
			},
		},

		// --- Administrative: operators ---
		{
			// Unauthenticated: registration is how an operator joins.
			pattern:    protocol.PathAdminOperatorsRegister,
			noFallback: true,
			methods: []muxMethod{
				{method: http.MethodPost, handler: o.HandleOperatorRegister},
			},
		},
		{
			// Unauthenticated by token: this is the endpoint that issues them.
			pattern:    protocol.PathAdminOperatorsToken,
			noFallback: true,
			methods: []muxMethod{
				{method: http.MethodPost, handler: o.HandleOperatorToken},
			},
		},
		{
			pattern: operators,
			methods: []muxMethod{
				{method: http.MethodGet, handler: o.HandleOperatorList},
			},
		},
		{
			pattern: operators + "/{name}",
			methods: []muxMethod{
				{method: http.MethodGet, handler: o.HandleOperatorGet},
				{method: http.MethodDelete, handler: o.HandleOperatorDelete},
			},
		},
		{
			pattern: operators + "/{name}/role",
			methods: []muxMethod{
				{method: http.MethodPut, handler: o.HandleOperatorRole},
			},
		},

		// --- Administrative: agents and overview ---
		{
			pattern: agents,
			methods: []muxMethod{
				{method: http.MethodGet, handler: o.HandleAdminAgents},
			},
		},
		{
			pattern: agents + "/{name}",
			methods: []muxMethod{
				{method: http.MethodGet, handler: o.HandleAdminAgentGet},
			},
		},
		{
			pattern: agents + "/{name}/deregister",
			methods: []muxMethod{
				{method: http.MethodPost, handler: o.HandleAdminAgentDeregister},
			},
		},
		{
			pattern: protocol.PathAdminOverview,
			methods: []muxMethod{
				{method: http.MethodGet, handler: o.HandleAdminOverview},
			},
		},
	}
}

// Routes registers every orchestrator endpoint on a fresh ServeMux using
// Go 1.22 method-and-pattern routes. Each path also gets a method-less
// pattern that answers a wrong method with a structured 405 and an Allow
// header, and an unmatched path answers with a structured 404 — a client
// that guesses wrong gets JSON back, never net/http's plain text.
func (o *Orchestrator) Routes() *http.ServeMux {
	mux := http.NewServeMux()

	for _, rt := range o.routeTable() {
		for _, m := range rt.methods {
			mux.HandleFunc(m.method+" "+rt.pattern, m.handler)
		}
		if rt.noFallback {
			continue
		}
		allowed := rt.allowed()
		mux.HandleFunc(rt.pattern, func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
			writeMethodNotAllowed(w, allowed...)
		})
	}

	mux.HandleFunc("/", o.handleNotFound)
	return mux
}

// handleNotFound answers an unrouted path with the registered NOT_FOUND
// code rather than an empty body.
func (o *Orchestrator) handleNotFound(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	protocol.WriteErrorCode(w, protocol.CodeNotFound,
		"no endpoint for "+r.Method+" "+observability.NormalizePath(r.URL.Path))
}

// Handler wraps the route mux in the observability middleware stack.
//
// Order, outermost first: trace, so a trace context exists (preserved from
// X-Trace-Id when the caller supplied one, generated when not) before
// anything else runs; metrics, so wl_http_requests_total and
// wl_http_request_duration_seconds count every request including those that
// end in 404 or 405; then the access log, which reads the trace context the
// outer layer established.
func (o *Orchestrator) Handler() http.Handler {
	var h http.Handler = o.Routes()
	h = o.logMiddleware(h)
	if o.Metrics != nil {
		h = observability.MetricsMiddleware(o.Metrics, h)
	}
	h = observability.TraceMiddleware(o.Logger, h)
	return h
}

// responseObserver captures the status code so the access log can report it.
type responseObserver struct {
	http.ResponseWriter
	status  int
	written bool
}

func (w *responseObserver) WriteHeader(status int) {
	if !w.written {
		w.status = status
		w.written = true
	}
	w.ResponseWriter.WriteHeader(status)
}

func (w *responseObserver) Write(b []byte) (int, error) {
	if !w.written {
		w.status = http.StatusOK
		w.written = true
	}
	return w.ResponseWriter.Write(b)
}

func (w *responseObserver) Flush() {
	if f, ok := w.ResponseWriter.(http.Flusher); ok {
		f.Flush()
	}
}

// logMiddleware emits one structured access line per request. The path is
// normalized so identifiers never reach a log field that would be joined to
// a metric label, and health and metrics polling logs at debug so a
// monitoring loop cannot flood the stream.
func (o *Orchestrator) logMiddleware(next http.Handler) http.Handler {
	return http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
		start := time.Now()
		rec := &responseObserver{ResponseWriter: w, status: http.StatusOK}

		next.ServeHTTP(rec, r)

		fields := map[string]any{
			"method":      r.Method,
			"path":        observability.NormalizePath(r.URL.Path),
			"status":      rec.status,
			"duration_ms": time.Since(start).Milliseconds(),
		}
		if tc, ok := observability.TraceFromContext(r.Context()); ok {
			fields["trace_id"] = tc.TraceID
			fields["span_id"] = tc.SpanID
		}

		switch {
		case rec.status >= http.StatusInternalServerError:
			o.Logger.Error("http request", fields)
		case rec.status >= http.StatusBadRequest:
			o.Logger.Warn("http request", fields)
		case isPollingPath(r.URL.Path):
			o.Logger.Debug("http request", fields)
		default:
			o.Logger.Info("http request", fields)
		}
	})
}

// isPollingPath reports whether a path is scraped on a schedule rather than
// requested by a peer doing work.
func isPollingPath(path string) bool {
	switch path {
	case protocol.PathHealth, protocol.PathMetrics:
		return true
	default:
		return false
	}
}

// Serve runs the orchestrator until ctx is cancelled or shutdown is
// requested, then drains in-flight requests within ShutdownGrace.
//
// The orchestrator is the first component a deployment starts, so a failure
// before the listener is open is fatal to the caller: Serve returns the
// error rather than degrading into a process that answers nothing.
func (o *Orchestrator) Serve(ctx context.Context) error {
	if ctx == nil {
		ctx = context.Background()
	}

	if !o.Started() {
		if err := o.Startup(ctx); err != nil {
			return fmt.Errorf("startup: %w", err)
		}
	}

	srv := &http.Server{
		Addr:              o.Config.Addr(),
		Handler:           o.Handler(),
		ReadHeaderTimeout: ReadHeaderTimeout,
		ReadTimeout:       ReadTimeout,
		WriteTimeout:      WriteTimeout,
		IdleTimeout:       IdleTimeout,
	}

	listener, err := net.Listen("tcp", srv.Addr)
	if err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("listen %s: %w", srv.Addr, err)
	}

	origin := o.Config.Origin()
	o.Logger.Info("orchestrator listening", map[string]any{
		"addr":       listener.Addr().String(),
		"url":        origin,
		"version":    o.Config.Version,
		"public_key": o.PublicKey(),
		"register":   protocol.JoinPath(origin, protocol.PathRegister),
		"services":   protocol.JoinPath(origin, protocol.PathServices),
		"health":     protocol.JoinPath(origin, protocol.PathHealth),
		"metrics":    protocol.JoinPath(origin, protocol.PathMetrics),
		"dev":        o.Config.DevMode(),
	})

	serveErr := make(chan error, 1)
	go func() {
		err := srv.Serve(listener)
		if errors.Is(err, http.ErrServerClosed) {
			err = nil
		}
		serveErr <- err
	}()

	var runErr error
	select {
	case runErr = <-serveErr:
		// The listener failed on its own; fall through and shut the rest down.
		if runErr != nil {
			o.Logger.Error("http server stopped", map[string]any{"error": runErr.Error()})
		}
	case <-ctx.Done():
		o.Logger.Info("shutdown requested", map[string]any{"reason": "context cancelled"})
	case <-o.Stopping():
		o.Logger.Info("shutdown requested", map[string]any{"reason": "orchestrator stopping"})
	}

	// Shutdown uses a fresh context: ctx may already be cancelled, and the
	// drain must still get its full grace period.
	shutdownCtx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), ShutdownGrace)
	defer cancel()

	if err := srv.Shutdown(shutdownCtx); err != nil {
		o.Logger.Warn("http shutdown incomplete", map[string]any{"error": err.Error()})
		if runErr == nil {
			runErr = fmt.Errorf("http shutdown: %w", err)
		}
		_ = srv.Close()
	}

	// Drain the serve goroutine so it cannot outlive this call.
	if err := <-serveErr; err != nil && runErr == nil {
		runErr = err
	}

	if err := o.Shutdown(shutdownCtx); err != nil {
		o.Logger.Error("orchestrator shutdown", map[string]any{"error": err.Error()})
		if runErr == nil {
			runErr = fmt.Errorf("shutdown: %w", err)
		}
	}

	o.Logger.Info("orchestrator stopped", map[string]any{"uptime": o.Uptime()})
	return runErr
}
